question: With Surgilogger force and camera-derived kinematics only, at what reconstruction accuracy does the Yeoh-vs-Ogden decision stop being recoverable?

truth.note: chosen, not measured; identifies nothing about real tissue

forward_model.specimen: slender tube in traction, non-uniform reference area
forward_model.equilibrium: P11(lambda(X)) * A(X) = F on every slice
forward_model.observable: gross stretch Lambda = mean of lambda(X)

arms.gated: shape pinned (yeoh c2=0.565, ogden alpha=4.247), stiffness fitted; needs the grasp phase logged as well as traction
arms.free: shape and stiffness both fitted to traction alone

area_scale_degeneracy.claim: area scale and G0 enter only as F/(G0*A), so a uniform area error is exactly compensated by the fitted stiffness and cannot affect which law wins

limitations: The truth is chosen. Nothing here says which law real tissue follows.
Reduced 1D specimen: no contact, mesh, solver, bending or torsion, so element quality and locking are untouched.
Both candidates and the synthetic truth are hyperelastic; a viscoelastic truth is NOT exercised, which makes these accuracies optimistic.
Injected errors are smooth and zero-mean in shape; real endoscopic reconstruction error is structured and may be worse.
Force noise is folded into the stretch residual rather than modelled on the force axis.
Quasi-static ramp only. The slip transient is excluded -- note 30 Hz video cannot resolve an event that needed 1 kHz force sampling.
Accuracy near 0.5 means the two laws are indistinguishable, not that the method failed.
